q: How does Chloe Martin want campaign lift reported for uncertainty?
a: As a point estimate with its 95% confidence interval; p-values are not shown in campaign readouts.

q: Which colour does Chloe Martin use to highlight the winning campaign, and why not brand blue?
a: Orange #E07B24; she avoids brand blue because blue series were read as 'baseline' in the Q3 2025 campaign readout.

q: What PSI trigger applies to credit-line (`cli-`) models in the monthly review now?
a: Above 0.20 on a top-20 feature since 2026-06-01; other model families keep 0.25.

q: What decimal places do risk-table default rates and PD use in the reporting convention?
a: 2 decimals in percent, e.g. 3.84%; other percentages use 1 decimal.

q: Where do the offer tiers come from?
a: The offers.tier_matrix table; tiers run A to E.

q: What interchange rate should I use for the book?
a: 1.9% blended; the 2.5% figure was the premium-card rate only.

q: Is OOT just the last three months of the training data?
a: No. OOT is a later period never used in training, tuning or feature selection; the last months of training data are in-time validation.

q: When does DPD start counting and what is day 1?
a: DPD counts from the payment due date. Per the 2026-01-15 fix, day 1 starts the day after the due date, and a payment posted on the due date still counts as current (0 DPD).

q: How do I report uplift from campaign response data that has a control group but was not randomised?
a: Do not report it as uplift; only randomised treatment and control holdouts give uplift. Report the difference as lift.

q: Why was the dispute-count feature rebuilt?
a: It read 14 days past the observation date, which inflated holdout AUC from 0.72 to 0.79; the rebuilt v2 reads only days on or before observation.
